name: AuthorLabel – EU AI Act Labels for AI Content & Chatbots
author: Stocked Labs

sections.description:
Article 50 of the EU AI Act has applied since 2 August 2026. It is the part of the law about telling people when they see AI-made content or talk to an AI.

It can concern your WordPress site if you:

  • show AI-generated or AI-edited images, video or audio that look real, for example product photos or “photos” in blog posts,
  • publish AI-written articles on news or public-interest topics without a human editor taking responsibility,
  • run an AI chatbot on your site (Tidio, Crisp, Intercom, AI Engine and similar).

Breaking Article 50 can be fined up to EUR 15 million or 3% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher. For SMEs and start-ups it is whichever is lower (Article 99). Each EU country’s market surveillance authority enforces it.

Most sites only need part of this. AuthorLabel asks six short questions, scans your plugins, and shows which Article 50 duties apply to your site, which do not, and which are your call. Then it adds the labels and notices for you, in a few clicks.

One place for the whole site. Your chatbot, your AI writing plugin and your image tool may each have their own disclosure setting, but each one only covers its own output. Text pasted from ChatGPT, images made elsewhere and uploaded to the media library, and older posts are covered by none of them. AuthorLabel keeps every AI label on your site in one place, in one consistent style, shows what still has no label, and logs who labelled what.

Built for European online shops (WooCommerce), blogs, news and magazine sites, and the agencies that run them. Free, no account, no external requests.

AuthorLabel is a tool, not legal advice. It helps you apply labels and keep a record of what you did. It does not certify compliance with any law. If you are unsure how the rules apply to your business, ask a lawyer.

In your language

AuthorLabel helps with what is often searched as: KI-Kennzeichnungspflicht and KI-Kennzeichnung (Deutsch), obligation de transparence IA and mention “contenu généré par IA” (Français), etiquetado de contenido generado por IA (Español), obblighi di trasparenza AI Act (Italiano), oznaczanie treści AI (Polski), AI-label voor AI-content (Nederlands).

What it does

  • First-run check. Six short questions plus an automatic scan of your plugins and scripts. You get a card listing each Article 50 duty as applies, does not apply or your call, with one sentence on why.
  • Chatbot notice. Tell visitors they are talking to AI: a footer bar, a small badge next to the chat widget, or a shortcode/block. Detects common chat widgets such as Tidio, Tawk.to, Crisp, Intercom, HubSpot and AI Engine. Optionally show it to EU visitors only, using your CDN’s country header (no external lookup).
  • Content labels. An “AI transparency” panel in the block editor, the classic editor and the media library. Mark a post, product or file as AI-generated, AI-assisted, reviewed by a human editor or not AI, and note the tool used.
  • Human review counts. Text that a named editor has reviewed and takes responsibility for is recorded as such, and is not given a public label.
  • Media detection. On upload, AuthorLabel reads C2PA, IPTC Digital Source Type and generator EXIF/XMP fields and suggests a label. It never guesses from writing style.
  • Visible and machine-readable labels. A badge or caption on the page, plus Schema.org JSON-LD, a meta tag and a data-ai-generated attribute. Your post content is never modified.
  • Bulk labelling. Filter by post type, date, author or tool and label up to 200 items at a time. Every bulk action can be undone.
  • “How we use AI” page. Generate an editable public page that explains your use of AI, and link it from the footer.
  • Readiness widget. A dashboard score from 0 to 100, what is done, what is left, and an action log of who labelled what and when.

AuthorLabel Pro

The free plugin covers everything listed above. AuthorLabel Pro is a separate, paid add-on for shops, teams and agencies that want less manual work and a clear record:

  • Automatic labels. A post is labelled as soon as an AI writing plugin generates text for it (AI Engine, GetGenie, Rank Math Content AI, Jetpack AI and others), so nobody has to remember.
  • Evidence report. A PDF and CSV report of what was labelled, when and by whom, to keep on file or share with a client.
  • Weekly email. A short summary of your readiness score and new content that still needs a label.
  • Agency branding and settings profiles. Your logo and colours on reports; copy settings between client sites.
  • AI-literacy register. Record who on your team was trained to use AI tools (Article 4).

Pro starts at $59 per year for one site. See Pro plans and pricing.

Pro is licensed through Freemius and checks its license key with Freemius. That is the only external request, and only Pro makes it. This plugin works fully without Pro.

Privacy

AuthorLabel makes no external requests. Labels, settings and the action log stay in your WordPress database. Nothing is sent to Stocked Labs or anyone else.

For developers

  • do_action( 'authorlabel_mark_content', $post_id, $status, $tool ) labels a post or attachment from your own code.
  • authorlabel_notice_text, authorlabel_badge_position and authorlabel_detectors filters change the notice text, badge position and detector list.

Full reference: authorlabel.com/docs.

Source code

The JavaScript in build/ is compiled from the files in src/, which ship with the plugin. To rebuild it, run npm install and npm run build in the plugin folder (requires Node.js 18.12 or later).
sections.installation:
1. Install from Plugins → Add New, or upload the authorlabel folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin. The first-run check opens automatically.
  3. Answer the questions, review the result, and turn on the labels that apply to you.
sections.faq:
My chatbot or AI plugin already has a disclosure setting. Do I still need this?

If that one tool is your only use of AI, its own setting may be enough. Most sites use several: a chat widget, a writing assistant, an image generator, text pasted from ChatGPT. AuthorLabel covers all of them in one place, finds content that has no label yet, and keeps a record. It works alongside those settings, not instead of them.

I run a small shop or blog. Does this concern me?

It can. Article 50 has no size limit: it depends on what you publish, not on how big you are. AI product photos that look like real photos, AI-made images in posts and an AI chat widget are the most common cases on small sites. Only the fine is capped lower for SMEs. The first-run check tells you which duties are likely to apply to your site.

Since when does this apply?

Article 50 has applied since 2 August 2026. Some providers of AI generation tools that were on the market before that date have until 2 December 2026 for the machine-readable marking duty in Article 50(2). The duties for sites that publish AI content and the chatbot duty were not delayed.

Does this make my site compliant with the EU AI Act?

No plugin can promise that. AuthorLabel shows which Article 50 duties are likely to concern your site, helps you add the labels and notices, and keeps a record. Whether that is enough for your situation is a legal question.

Do I have to label every AI-assisted blog post?

Not always. Article 50(4) covers AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest, and it does not apply when a human editor has reviewed the text and takes editorial responsibility. AuthorLabel lets you record that review. Spell-checking does not count as editorial review.

My chatbot vendor already says it is AI. Do I still need a notice?

The duty in Article 50(1) sits mainly with the chatbot provider. Many vendor notices are small or hidden, so AuthorLabel offers a visible notice as an extra, optional step. The first-run check marks this as your call.

Does AuthorLabel detect AI text automatically?

It records AI use when a supported AI writing tool reports it (Pro adds automatic labelling for several tools). It does not try to guess from writing style, because style-based detectors are unreliable.

What happens to my labels if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Labels are stored as post meta and stay with your content. Settings and the action log are removed on deletion only if you tick that option.
